news.title: Pressure on Gianni Infantino increases as Uefa members prepare to oppose re-election
news.lede: European nations to withdraw letters of support for Fifa president. Appetite to ensure Infantino is quickly removed from post. European countries are planning to increase the pressure on Gianni Infantino with a mass withdrawal of letters supporting his re-election as Fifa president. Infantino’s reign is in severe peril after the collapse of his privately backed scheme to sell off chunks of the World Cup, which was largely scuppered when Uefa member associations threatened to boycott future Fifa competitions.

news.title: Real Madrid backs FIFA’s World Cup stake sale U-turn
news.lede: Real Madrid have backed FIFA‘s decision to withdraw plans to sell a minority stake in the commercial rights of the men’s and women’s World Cups, as pressure mounted on FIFA president Gianni Infantino over the controversial proposal. The 15-time UEFA Champions League winners described the move as “good news for football” after widespread opposition forced FIFA to abandon plans to open its flagship competitions to private investors. Read Also: UEFA threatens FIFA boycott over Infantino’s plan to sell World Cup stake Real Madrid backs FIFA U-turn. Infantino’s proposal had sought to create a new commercial entity through which FIFA would sell minority stakes in the commercial rights of its major tournaments, including the men’s and women’s World Cups.

news.title: Bruno Guimaraes: From Brazil's World Cup villain to the verge of Arsenal's record signing
news.lede: Just weeks after being singled out for Brazil's painful World Cup exit, Bruno Guimaraes is set to become Arsenal's record signing in a reported £80 million move from Newcastle United. The Brazil midfielder, who endured intense criticism after missing a crucial penalty in his country's last-16 defeat to Norway, is expected to sign a five-year contract until 2031, subject to a medical and official confirmation from both clubs. Guimaraes was one of Carlo Ancelotti's standout performers throughout the tournament, but his campaign became defined by one moment. With Brazil level against Norway in the round of 16, the 28-year-old saw his first-half penalty, awarded after a foul on Matheus Cunha, saved by goalkeeper Orjan Nyland.

news.title: Football: Soccer-FIFA must rebuild trust after scrapping World Cup investor proposal, says Boyce
news.lede: Aug 2 (Reuters) - Former FIFA vice-president Jim Boyce ⁠said on Sunday world soccer's governing body should focus on the interests of fans after President Gianni Infantino abandoned plans to sell ⁠a stake in the World Cup to private investors, calling the proposal "ludicrous". FIFA had proposed raising up to $4.2 billion by selling a ‌roughly 20% stake in a new entity that would oversee FIFA competitions, including the World Cup. The proposal, unveiled on Tuesday, drew immediate backlash. European football's governing body UEFA threatened to boycott FIFA events and accused the organisation of putting the sport's "soul" up for sale.

news.title: Football Ferns legend breaks silence on controversial call to miss 2023 Women's World Cup
news.lede: Reminder, this is a Premium article and requires a subscription to read. Former Football Ferns captain Abby Erceg, pictured during one of her last international appearances. Former Football Ferns captain Abby Erceg has no regrets over her absence from the 2023 Fifa Women’s World Cup in New Zealand and Australia, even if it was one of the toughest decisions of her career. Erceg, who will feature as a guest player for Auckland FC’s invitational team against Chelsea Women on Saturday at Eden Park, was the biggest name missing from Jitka Klimkova’s squad three years ago.

news.title: Trump watches on as football explodes
news.lede: Being FIFA president carries an undeniable political dimension. “He looks like a prime minister,” people often say of Infantino when he appears at tournaments or FIFA Congresses. The power of the organisation he leads, and of the industry it represents, is immense. Infantino has dealt with major political figures in that sphere, from Vladimir Putin ahead of the 2018 World Cup to the Emir of Qatar and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for the 2022 and 2034 tournaments respectively.

news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.
